The saved ASan report records `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at `src/libespeak-ng/encoding.c:539:15`, with the faulting address `0x602000000153` located `0` bytes to the right of the 3-byte `..\0` heap region allocated by `tests/ssml-fuzzer.c`.

Source. `text_decoder_decode_string_multibyte()` reaches this helper with `length < 0`, so synchronous synthesis measures the attacker-controlled NUL-terminated witness itself. For the saved `..\0` string, `length` becomes `3`.

The helper selects the UTF-8 getter and initializes the decoder over the exact three-byte range `[string, string + 3)`: first dot, second dot, appended NUL. Later EOF checks compare `decoder->current` against this `decoder->end` pointer.
`ReadClause()` fetches the first byte from `p_decoder` into lookahead `c2`. On the witness this returns the first `'.'` and advances `decoder->current` to the second byte.
At the top of the loop, the first dot stored in `c2` becomes the current punctuation character `c1`.
`GetC()` reads the second `'.'` into lookahead `c2`. `Eof()` is still false immediately afterward, so the appended NUL remains the next unread decoder byte.

The repeated-dot probe tests for a third dot. For the exact `..\0` witness, its `GetC()` consumes the in-bounds NUL, returns `0`, never enters the loop body, and `UngetC(0)` leaves nothing queued back; `p_decoder.current` is now equal to `p_decoder.end` while `c1` and `c2` still hold the two dots.
The first dot is classified as `CLAUSE_PERIOD`. That value is a composite clause bitfield, not a dedicated one-bit tag.

This guard is still true for `CLAUSE_PERIOD`, because `CLAUSE_QUESTION` and `CLAUSE_EXCLAMATION` are composite constants that share the sentence and pause bits present in `CLAUSE_PERIOD`. Control therefore enters the punctuation-run scan even though the current character is `'.'`.

Root-cause step. `c2` is still the second `'.'`, so the same composite-bit test keeps the loop header true. Because the header lacks the patch's `!Eof()` check, the loop proceeds even though step 6 already left `p_decoder.current == p_decoder.end`.
The loop body now calls `GetC()` at EOF. The saved ASan stack records this exact caller site (`ReadClause:798`) flowing into `GetC:174` and `text_decoder_getc:769` with the exhausted decoder state.

Sink. Because step 10 reaches the UTF-8 backend with `decoder->current == decoder->end`, this dereference reads one byte past the 3-byte `..\0` heap buffer, exactly as reported by the saved ASan trace.

First project-side materialization of vulnerability-relevant input state. The synchronous text decoder ignores the harness `size` and recomputes the attacker-controlled string length from the NUL-terminated witness buffer itself.
Missing EOF guard on the punctuation-run scan. Once `c2` still holds `'.'` and the decoder has already reached EOF, this loop still stays true and permits another `GetC()` from the exhausted buffer.
ASan sink. After `ReadClause()` has already advanced the decoder to EOF, the UTF-8 backend dereferences `decoder->current` at `decoder->end` and reads one byte past the heap-backed witness string.
